clue.text: Birds on seaside spot to start with, eating what they eat

indicators.note: to start with asks for only the opening letter of each of the three words before it
something eating takes food inside it, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: first letter of on
first letter of seaside
birds of prey eat their prey
first letter of spot

explanation.surface: Seabirds at a beach spot are tucking into their usual meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters O, S, S are split so that PREY sits between the second and third: OS + PREY + S.
explanation.definitionFit: Ospreys are fish-eating raptors, a kind of bird.

indicators.note: caught in the sense of heard, as when you catch what someone says

blocks.note: a vulgar word for something awful
a menagerie is a collection of animals, a zoo

explanation.surface: A dog has been trapped inside a dreadful animal collection.
explanation.walkthrough: A rude homophone: say 'shit zoo' and you get the breed's name. Chambers allows it as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The shih-tzu is a small long-haired toy breed of dog from Tibet and China.

clue.text: Realism is lost in this field

indicators.note: says the two letters spelling is go missing from the longer word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the part to remove

explanation.surface: Realism has no place in this particular area of art or thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing IS from REALISM leaves REALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or sphere of activity, just as a field is.

clue.text: We read out a couple of letters

indicators.note: reading something out means voicing it, so the sounds matter rather than the spelling

blocks.note: two letters of the alphabet, U and I, spoken together

explanation.surface: Two of us recite a pair of letters aloud together.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the letters U and I sound like the pronouns 'you and I'.
explanation.definitionFit: We is the pronoun meaning the speaker plus another person, which is you and I.

clue.text: Dealing with cake that's seasonal without filling and topping

indicators.note: a word without its filling has its middle emptied out, keeping just its outer shell

blocks.note: seasonal with its inside removed
the sugary topping on a cake

explanation.surface: Someone handles a festive cake that has no filling and no topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling and topping' reads like two things missing from the cake, but 'and' just joins two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a cake into portions is slicing it, so slicing is what you do when dealing with one.

blocks.note: surface: a person's face, lying on a pillow
setter's reading: a face is a clock dial, and that word written upwards in a down light gives the answer's first word

explanation.surface: Someone's face looks unwell as they lie in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A face is a DIAL; in a down entry, DIAL written from the bottom up reads LAID, so it is literally LAID UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To be laid up is to be confined to bed by illness or injury.

blocks.note: one big boat that carries cargo boxes
setter's reading: both halves of the answer are themselves vessels, a receptacle and a boat

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is one vessel, or two vessels written side by side: a container is a vessel in the receptacle sense, and a ship in the nautical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A container ship is a large cargo vessel built to carry standard shipping containers.

blocks.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
a whiff is a smell or scent

explanation.surface: A faint smell of sodium is starting to appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into being, beginning to develop.

indicators.note: original in the sense of novel or inventive, so the letters are freshly rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written: the mathematician's name plus a and notable

explanation.surface: Praise for the great mathematician Euler as a remarkable, inventive figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A tongue-in-cheek &lit: Euler (1707-83) died over a century before the first Nobel prizes in 1901, and there is no Nobel for mathematics, hence the exclamation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nobel laureate is a distinguished prize-winner, the sort of notable original the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Singer keen to make a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word travels back the way it came

blocks.note: keen means eager, avid

explanation.surface: A vocalist is eager to return to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: To split up and desert over the onset of marriage is an idealised vision

indicators.note: to split something is to go into the middle of it, dividing it in two
turned over, so the word is read from the other end
an onset is a beginning, so only the first letter is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Sinai is the desert peninsula of Egypt
first letter of marriage

explanation.surface: Breaking up and abandoning someone at the start of a marriage is a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a verb about walking out; it is the noun, the Sinai.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopianism is belief in, or pursuit of, an ideal perfect society, an idealised vision of the world.

clue.text: Testament featuring male member in bloomers

indicators.note: a word featuring something has it included within itself

blocks.note: sits inside the word, between its first two and last letters

explanation.surface: A cheeky reference to a man's anatomy in someone's knickers, given as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers are flowers here, not old-fashioned knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-bearing male organ of a flower, and bloomers are flowers.

clue.text: Followed the example of having dealt poorly with bird

indicators.note: done poorly means badly handled, so the letters end up out of order

blocks.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone copied a card player who had dealt badly with a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate is to imitate someone you admire, copying their conduct.

clue.text: Regular light infantry starts out with one who doesn't belong

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters
out in the sense of wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
first letters of light and infantry

explanation.surface: Regular soldiers set out alongside an outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular light infantry' reads as one military unit, yet regular is the fodder for its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular fighter, outside any official army, so does not belong to the regular forces.

indicators.note: a production is something made or staged, so the letters are reworked into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A channel revives an old television show.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrieval is the act of fetching something and recovering it.

blocks.note: first meaning: tangles tied in rope or hair
second meaning: units of speed at sea, nautical miles per hour

explanation.walkthrough: Speed is a fair definition because the nautical unit, in the plural, is used to give a rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Knots are both twisted tangles and the measure of a ship's or aircraft's velocity.

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside

blocks.note: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British hospital casualty department
a laceration is a cut

explanation.surface: A sharp pain from a gash being treated in the emergency ward.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the hospital emergency department is called casualty or A&E.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute means keen or sharp, as in acute pain or an acute angle.

clue.text: Wine and tea and endless joy

indicators.note: with no end, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: cha (or char) is a British slang word for tea
bliss is perfect joy

explanation.surface: A list of life's pleasures: wine, a cuppa and boundless happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white wine from the Burgundy region of France.

indicators.note: activity implies lively movement, so the letters are stirred about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A busy stadium laid on for our benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' looks like a throwaway word but is the whole definition: all of humanity.
explanation.definitionFit: We people collectively are humankind, so 'us' stands for the whole species.

clue.text: Booze trashed what's within school walls

indicators.note: what lies within a word is its interior, without its outermost letters
something trashed is wrecked, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: school without its first and last letters
walls without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Drink that got students wrecked inside the school grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trashed' tempts as slang for drunk alongside booze, but it is the anagram signal; 'school walls' is two words, each losing its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is the informal word for alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Covers eyes, we hear, to turn over

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of the word rather than how it is spelt

blocks.note: caps are covers or lids
the word eyes, spoken

explanation.surface: Someone shields their eyes, apparently, in order to roll over.
explanation.definitionFit: When a boat capsizes it overturns in the water.

indicators.note: an instruction not to begin, so the word's first letter is dropped

blocks.note: clashes are arguments or disputes

explanation.surface: A plea to avoid starting rows and fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashes are strokes with a whip, so a flogging is a series of beatings.

blocks.note: surface: a badge or emblem awarded to someone
setter's reading: split the answer as three words and it describes the letters of a badge, with one word sitting inside another

explanation.surface: Someone is awarded a badge for clowning about.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as BAD IN AGE and you get A BADGE, since BAD sits in AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, teasing banter, a kind of verbal fooling around.

blocks.note: can means is able to
to ape is to mimic or simulate

explanation.surface: A starter dish that can pass itself off as something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury bite served before a meal as an hors d'oeuvre.

clue.text: Finally clean a dirty place that's vile

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: last letter of clean
taken as written
a pigsty, the classic filthy place

explanation.surface: At last someone cleans up a filthy, repulsive spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and vile are synonyms, both meaning thoroughly unpleasant or disgusting.

clue.text: One of 16 churches: the first welcomes love, the second follows it

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside
says which piece comes after which in the line

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church; this is the first of two
taken as written
taken as written
the second church abbreviation

explanation.surface: Two churches, one embracing love and the other trailing after it.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 across is KNOTS; C(LOVE)H + IT + CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove hitch is a common knot used to fasten a rope to a post.

definitions.note: a verb phrase, read as two words: use less

blocks.note: first meaning: pointless, having no effect
second meaning: split into two words, to consume a smaller amount

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning only works with a space: to cut back on something is to USE LESS of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futile achieves nothing, so it is of no use at all.

blocks.note: a play is a drama
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A playwright's refuge from the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is an enclosure where a small child can play in safety.
